messages:
jordan: heads up — since ~02:10 UTC we've had a preemption wave in eu-west1 GPU pool. lots of tiny free GPU slots appearing but large jobs (>=4g) are stuck pending and then getting evicted repeatedly. grafana: https://grafana.redwood-infra/eu-west1/gpu-preemptions :sadpanda:

maya: ugh. any obvious correlate? node upgrades, spot terminations, autoscaler?

jordan: not node upgrades. spot term diff looks normal. autoscaler logs show a bunch of small nodes created then drained. suspect fragmentation from reserved capacity for dedicated customers + bursty batch jobs.

sanjay: can you paste a couple of pod events? curious if it's "Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu" or preemption by taint/priority.

jordan: paste of kubectl output below (truncated):
```
$ kubectl get pods -n batch -o wide
NAME                          READY  STATUS     RESTARTS  AGE   NODE
embedder-v2-7f9c8d6b4-2z3kq  0/1    Evicted     0        9m   gpu-node-eu-12
trainer-big-0                 0/1    Pending     0        3m   <none>
batch-worker-5                1/1    Running     0        45m  gpu-node-eu-21
```
Events for trainer-big-0:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  30s  default-scheduler  0/10 nodes are available: 10 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
```

jordan: nodes show 0.5-1.5 GPUs free in many places. it's classic fragmentation: lots of 1 GPU pods spread out, large jobs need 4 contiguous gpus and scheduler can't pack them.

olivia: agreed — this is where our current topologySpread + prefer-affinity tradeoff hurts packing. we bias for spreading for reliability (too many single-gpu pods across AZs) so we lose contiguity for multi-gpu.

maya: short-term mitigation: can we temporary flip a scheduler predicate to prefer binpack for batch queue? or add a packingPriority for multi-gpu. low risk if only for batch namespace.

sanjay: yup—two options: 1) a quick scheduler tweak to weight "least-allocatable-gpu" (prefer packing) for batch namespace. 2) an infra job to consolidate: cordon small underutilized nodes, drain lightweight jobs (best-effort) onto denser nodes, then deprovision empty ones. 1 is lower-touch but affects scheduling behaviour; 2 is more surgical but requires safe eviction (pdbs).

jordan: option 2 looks safest for SLAs. can infra run a controlled defrag run during our low-traffic window (03:30 UTC)?

olivia: we can run a "consolidator" playbook — mark nodes with label gpu-frag=1, cordon, and migrate non-critical pods. will need sign-off from SRE and owners for any pdb overrides.

infra-bot: scheduled maintenance window created by olivia at 03:30 UTC: playbook/consolidate-gpu-pools v1. Action: cordon/drain small-nodes-eu-west1 (ETA 25m).

maya: ops checklist: 1) ensure batch jobs have lower priorityClass or toleration so they are evicted first; 2) set auto-scheduler backoff to 10s (shorter) while run happening; 3) monitor tail latencies for embedder service.

sanjay: cost note: consolidation will increase short-term pod churn and transient GPU-hours while migrating, but should reduce long-term tail scheduling time and reduce spot churn. expected payback ~48-72h for eu-west pool.

jordan: thanks. please keep this thread updated. if consolidator can't complete automatically we fallback to scheduler-weight change. @eng-sre please watch SLAs on embedder and batch. :thumbsup:

olivia: ack, starting dry-run now, will post logs here.

jordan: posted dry-run output: most small nodes drained successfully, 3 pods needed manual pdb override (raising priority temporarily). consolidation reduced pending 4g job wait from ~12m to ~90s in test.

maya: awesome, roll it during window. will prepare rollback steps for schedule-weight flip if anything goes sideways.

sanjay: after consolidation we should add periodic defrag cron (weekly) and consider a scheduler plugin to prefer contiguous GPU allocation for multi-gpu pods. file a follow-up RFC?

jordan: filing RFC after window: will include metrics and cost delta.

olivia: dry-run logs: https://artifacts.redwood-infra/defrag/eu-west1/dryrun-1934567890.log

infra-bot: maintenance completed (dry-run) — 12 nodes drained, 9 deprovision candidates identified.

jordan: closing loop — moving to scheduled run at 03:30 UTC. will report back with final numbers.
